docs.title: HTTP Utilities
docs.text: Standardization of RESTful responses.

docs.title: Why This Package Exists
docs.text: In a system with dozens of API endpoints, inconsistency in response headers, status codes, or payload formats leads to brittle clients. The httputil package ensures that every HTTP response from the manager-service follows the same "look and feel."

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
This package provides a simple wrapper around the standard net/http library.

sequenceDiagram
    participant H as Handler
    participant U as httputil.WriteJSON
    participant W as ResponseWriter

    H->>U: WriteJSON(w, 200, payload)
    U->>U: json.Marshal(payload)
    alt Success
        U->>W: Set Content-Type: application/json
        U->>W: WriteHeader(200)
        U->>W: Write(body + \n)
    else Marshal Error
        U->>W: WriteHeader(500)
        U->>W: Write("failed to encode response")
    end

docs.title: JSON-First Communication
docs.text: All structured data returned by the system is JSON. This simplifies integration with the CLI and any future web dashboards.

docs.title: CLI Friendliness
docs.text: By appending \n to every JSON response, the utilities ensure that users running curl in their terminal get a clean prompt on the next line, rather than having the JSON blob merged with their shell prompt.

docs.title: WriteJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, payload any) error
docs.text: The workhorse function for the UI Service. It handles content negotiation (fixing it to JSON), status code setting, and serialization in one call.

docs.title: WriteErrorJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, message string)
docs.text: Sends a structured JSON error response following the standard error contract {"error": "...", "code": 400}.

docs.title: Error Catalogue
docs.text: Error Meaning Recovery failed to encode response The Go struct could not be marshaled to JSON (e.g., recursive reference). This is a developer error; check the struct tags and types.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
func MyHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    data := GetSomeData()
    if err := httputil.WriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, data); err != nil {
        log.Printf("Failed to write response: %v", err)
    }
}

docs.title: manager
docs.text: Core scheduling and orchestration logic for KubeMapReduce jobs.

docs.title: Why This Package Exists
docs.text: The MapReduce Manager is the brain of the cluster. Without it, work would not be distributed, and there would be no way to coordinate the complex Map-then-Reduce phase sequencing. This package ensures that if a worker fails, its task is automatically rescheduled, and that "zombie" workers cannot corrupt the output of a job.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The following flowchart shows the high-level logic used in GetNextTask to assign work while enforcing phase barriers and resource quotas.

flowchart TD
    Start([GetNextTask Request]) --> Lock[Acquire Scheduling Lock]
    Lock --> Quota{Quota Available?}
    Quota -- No --> ErrQ[ErrQuotaExceeded]
    Quota -- Yes --> MapIdle{Map Task Idle?}
    MapIdle -- Yes --> AssignMap[Assign Map Task]
    MapIdle -- No --> MapDone{Map Phase Complete?}
    MapDone -- No --> WaitMap[ErrNoIdleTasks]
    MapDone -- Yes --> RedIdle{Reduce Task Idle?}
    RedIdle -- Yes --> AssignRed[Assign Reduce Task]
    RedIdle -- No --> RedDone{Reduce Phase Complete?}
    RedDone -- Yes --> Done[ErrJobCompleted]
    RedDone -- No --> WaitRed[ErrNoIdleTasks]
    AssignMap --> Commit[Commit Transaction]
    AssignRed --> Commit
    Commit --> Finish([Return Task Assignment])

The "Active Reaper" (FailStaleTasks) runs as a background loop to reclaim tasks from workers that have stopped heartbeating.

flowchart TD
    RStart([Reaper Loop]) --> Scan[Scan In-Progress Tasks]
    Scan --> Expired{Lease Expired?}
    Expired -- No --> Next[Next Task]
    Expired -- Yes --> Retry{Attempts < Max?}
    Retry -- Yes --> Resched[Move to Idle & Re-spawn]
    Retry -- No --> FailJob[Fail Entire Job]
    Resched --> Next
    FailJob --> Next

docs.title: Lease-Based Fencing
docs.text: When a worker is assigned a task, it receives an attempt_id and a lease_id. - The attempt_id is a unique identifier for that specific try. It must be sent with every RPC (Heartbeat, TaskComplete). The Manager will reject any RPC where the attempt_id does not match the current_attempt_id in the DDS. - The lease_id is a secondary token that must match the lease_id stored for that specific attempt. It is refreshed during every Heartbeat.

docs.title: State Transitions
docs.text: Tasks follow a strict linear progression: Idle → InProgress → Completed (or back to Idle on failure). These transitions are guarded by atomic database transactions that lock the task row (FOR UPDATE), preventing race conditions between concurrent Managers or a Manager and a Worker.

docs.title: Manager Partitioning
docs.text: In a multi-replica deployment, each Manager instance is responsible for a subset of the jobs based on a hash of the jobID. This ensures that a single Manager instance owns the lifecycle of a job, simplifying the logic for phase transitions and cleanup.

docs.title: Exported API
docs.text: Function/Type Signature Description Scheduler struct Central coordinator for job and task lifecycles. NewScheduler func(...) (*Scheduler, error) Initializes a new scheduler with a DB connection and orchestrator. GetNextTask func(...) (*Task, error) Atomically assigns the next available task to a worker. CompleteTask func(...) error Marks a task as successfully completed and persists output URIs. FailTask func(...) error Signals a task failure and triggers a retry or job-wide failure. RenewLease func(...) error Extends a task's validity window based on a worker's heartbeat. FailStaleTasks func(...) (int, error) Reclaims tasks from workers that have stopped heartbeating.

docs.title: Error Catalogue
docs.text: Error Meaning ErrNoIdleTasks All tasks for the current phase are already assigned. ErrStaleAttempt A worker tried to commit/heartbeat for an attempt that is no longer current. ErrExpiredLease The worker's lease has timed out in the DDS. ErrQuotaExceeded The cluster has reached the maximum allowed concurrent pods. ErrJobFailed One or more tasks reached the maximum retry attempts.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
// Initialize a scheduler
orchestrator := manager.NewKubeOrchestrator(clientset, "mapreduce", "worker:latest")
scheduler, _ := manager.NewScheduler(db, 0, 1, orchestrator, "manager:50051", 30)

// Periodically run the Active Reaper in the background
go func() {
    for {
        count, _ := scheduler.FailStaleTasks(context.Background())
        if count > 0 {
            log.Printf("Reclaimed %d stale tasks", count)
        }
        time.Sleep(10 * time.Second)
    }
}()

// Assign a task to a worker
task, err := scheduler.GetNextTask(ctx, jobID, workerID)
if err != nil {
    // Handle error (e.g., ErrNoIdleTasks or ErrJobCompleted)
}

docs.title: models
docs.text: Central data structures and Distributed Data Store (DDS) schemas.

docs.title: Why This Package Exists
docs.text: The models package acts as the "lingua franca" of the KubeMapReduce system. Without it, the Manager, Workers, and API would have disparate views of what a "Job" or "Task" is, leading to marshalling errors and database inconsistencies. It provides the strong typing required to safely pass state across gRPC and REST boundaries.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
erDiagram
    JOBS ||--o{ TASKS : "contains"
    JOBS ||--|| JOB_CONFIGS : "configured by"
    TASKS ||--o{ TASK_INPUTS : "has"
    TASKS ||--o{ TASK_ATTEMPTS : "executed as"
    TASKS ||--o{ TASK_OUTPUTS : "produces"

    JOBS {
        uuid job_id PK
        string status "Pending|Running|Completed|Failed|Cancelled"
        timestamp created_at
    }
    TASKS {
        uuid task_id PK
        uuid job_id FK
        string task_type "Map|Reduce"
        uuid current_attempt_id FK
    }
    TASK_ATTEMPTS {
        uuid attempt_id PK
        uuid task_id FK
        uuid lease_id
        timestamp last_renewed_at
    }

docs.title: Distributed Data Store (DDS) Mapping
docs.text: Most types in this package include db tags, indicating a direct 1:1 mapping with a PostgreSQL table. This ensures that the code's view of the world is perfectly aligned with the persistent state stored in the DDS.

docs.title: Status Enumerations
docs.text: The package defines several string-based types (JobStatus, TaskStatus, AttemptStatus) to represent state machines. Using custom types instead of raw strings prevents accidental state transitions and enables compile-time checking of valid states.

docs.title: Fencing via current_attempt_id
docs.text: The Task struct's CurrentAttemptID field is the cornerstone of the system's "fencing" strategy. By only accepting results from the attempt that matches this ID, the system prevents "zombie" workers from corrupting data.

docs.title: Exported API
docs.text: Type/Func Description Job Root entity for a MapReduce workflow. Task A single unit of work (Map or Reduce partition). TaskAttempt Represents one execution instance of a Task. JobSubmissionRequest API payload for submitting new jobs. IsTerminal() Helper to check if a job has finished (Success/Fail/Cancel).

docs.text: This package is data-only and does not return errors. Validation logic is located in the internal/validation package.

job := models.Job{
    JobID:  uuid.New(),
    UserID: userID,
    Status: models.JobPending,

docs.title: Shuffle
docs.text: High-performance k-way merge sort for intermediate MapReduce data.

docs.title: Why This Package Exists
docs.text:
In a distributed MapReduce system, individual Mapper tasks produce sorted fragments of data. A Reducer task, however, requires a single, globally sorted stream of all records assigned to its partition.

The shuffle package solves the "Shuffle" problem: aggregating hundreds or thousands of sorted JSONL files into one stream without exhausting the Manager's memory or file descriptor limits. It ensures that the Reducer receives data in a strictly deterministic, sorted order, which is an invariant required for the Reduce function to operate correctly on keyed groups.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The following flowchart describes the multi-pass external merge logic used to handle datasets larger than RAM and stream counts larger than the system's file descriptor limit.

graph TD
    Start[MergeInputs Start] --> CheckCount{Stream Count > BatchSize?}
    CheckCount -- Yes --> MultiPass[Multi-pass Merge]
    CheckCount -- No --> SinglePass[Single-pass Heap Merge]

    MultiPass --> Split[Split into batches of size BatchSize]
    Split --> MergeBatch[Merge each batch into temporary spill file]
    MergeBatch --> Collect[Collect spill files as new input list]
    Collect --> CheckCount

    SinglePass --> HeapInit[Initialize Min-Heap with first record of each stream]
    HeapInit --> Pop[Pop smallest record from Heap]
    Pop --> Write[Write record to output]
    Write --> Scan[Scan next record from the same stream]
    Scan --> Push[Push next record to Heap]
    Push --> Empty{Heap Empty?}
    Empty -- No --> Pop
    Empty -- Yes --> End[Finish]

docs.title: External K-Way Merge
docs.text: Standard merge sort works in memory. External merge sort spills intermediate results to disk. This package uses a container/heap based min-heap to always pick the smallest key across all open streams, ensuring $O(N \log K)$ performance where $N$ is total records and $K$ is the number of streams.

docs.title: Multi-Pass Spilling
docs.text: To prevent EMFILE (Too many open files) errors, the package implements recursive spilling. If you try to merge 2000 files but the BatchSize is 500, it will perform 4 merges of 500 files each, creating 4 intermediate "spill" files, and then merge those 4 files in a final pass.

docs.title: Stable Merging
docs.text: By tracking the index of the input stream in the heap, the package ensures that if two records have identical keys, they are emitted in the order of the input streams, maintaining stability.

docs.title: MergeInputs(readers []io.Reader, w io.Writer, cfg MergeConfig) (MergeStats, error)
docs.text: The primary entry point. It orchestrates the entire merge process, handling both single-pass optimizations and multi-pass recursive spilling.

docs.title: MergeConfig
docs.text: Tunables for the merge operation. - BatchSize: Maximum concurrent open files (default 500). - TempDir: Location for intermediate spill files.

docs.title: Record
docs.text: The data contract. Each record must be a JSON object with key and value strings.

docs.title: Error Catalogue
docs.text: Error Meaning Recovery failed to create spill file Disk full or permissions issue in TempDir. Check disk space and MergeConfig.TempDir. malformed JSON in stream A Mapper produced invalid JSONL. Check Mapper output logic; data is corrupted. failed to encode output The output writer (e.g., a network stream or file) failed. Check Reducer availability or disk health.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
cfg := shuffle.DefaultMergeConfig()
stats, err := shuffle.MergeInputs(mapperOutputs, reducerInput, cfg)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatalf("Shuffle failed: %v", err)
}
fmt.Printf("Merged %d records in %d passes\n", stats.TotalRecords, stats.TotalPasses)

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Request sanitization and system invariant enforcement.

docs.title: Why This Package Exists
docs.text:
Distributed systems are fragile when faced with malformed input. A single job submission with a path traversal string could compromise the Manager's filesystem, or a Reducer count of -1 could crash the scheduler's logic.

The validation package acts as the system's "immune system." It ensures that every request entering the manager-service is checked against security rules (path sanitization) and operational rules (interface contracts) before any resources are committed.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The following flowchart shows how validation is integrated into the job submission lifecycle.

graph TD
    API[HTTP Handler] --> Call[validation.ValidateJobSubmission]
    Call --> PathCheck{Path is Safe?}
    PathCheck -- No --> Fail[Return BadRequestError]
    PathCheck -- Yes --> InterfaceCheck{Interfaces Match?}
    InterfaceCheck -- No --> Fail
    InterfaceCheck -- Yes --> ResourceCheck{Resource counts > 0?}
    ResourceCheck -- No --> Fail
    ResourceCheck -- Yes --> Pass[Job Accepted -> Scheduler]
    Fail --> Resp[HTTP 400 Bad Request]

docs.title: Path Sanitization
docs.text: The system uses filepath.Clean and manual checks to ensure that filename fields only contain simple base names. This prevents Path Traversal attacks, ensuring that a Worker or Manager can only ever read from or write to the designated data/ or output/ directories.

docs.title: Interface Contracts
docs.text: KubeMapReduce supports multiple languages (Python, Java, C++). To ensure that a Mapper artifact written in Python can actually be called by the Worker, the validation package enforces a strict interface string match (e.g., map(key,value)->[]KeyValue).

docs.title: Error Classification
docs.text: By wrapping validation failures in the BadRequestError type, the system distinguishes between "the user made a mistake" (400) and "the server failed" (500).

docs.title: ValidateJobSubmission(req models.JobSubmissionRequest) error
docs.text: Validates a full MapReduce job. It checks paths, languages, artifacts, and resource requirements.

docs.title: ValidateCreateUserRequest(req models.CreateUserRequest) error
docs.text: Validates user creation payloads, ensuring role canonicalization via NormalizeRole.

docs.title: BadRequestError
docs.text: A specific error type that indicates a client-side validation failure.

docs.title: Error Catalogue
docs.text: Error Meaning Recovery filename is invalid The user attempted to use .. or an absolute path. Use a simple filename like input.jsonl. language must be one of... Unsupported runtime requested. Choose from python, java, c, or cpp. interface must be... The artifact signature does not match the task type. Correct the interface string in the job spec. reducers must be a positive integer Invalid resource count. Request 1 or more Reducers.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
err := validation.ValidateJobSubmission(request)
